features.name: Go ownership
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter establishes substantial, central experience building production systems in Go, the role's required backend language.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or only appears as a bare keyword with no evidence of use.
Go is mentioned among several languages, but the letter does not show it as a core production language.
Go is described as a main language used on production services.
Go is presented as the applicant's primary or daily language, tied to concrete backend design, implementation, or operational ownership.

features.evidence: My Python is production-grade, not just scripting
features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures the extent to which the letter shows Python as a serious production engineering language rather than incidental scripting.

levels.descriptor: Python is not mentioned.
Python is mentioned only briefly or as a light scripting tool.
The letter shows regular Python use for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
The letter shows deep, production-grade Python ownership, such as typed or tested services, broad internal tooling, or heavy operational reliance.

features.name: Applied AI experience
features.description: Captures whether the applicant shows hands-on experience deploying AI or language-model functionality in production and understanding its reliability constraints.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
AI is mentioned only as an interest area or vague exposure.
The letter shows hands-on work shipping model-backed or LLM-based features.
The letter shows shipped AI systems plus evaluation, guardrails, or explicit attention to failure modes and trustworthy deployment.

features.evidence: led security reviews of services I did not write
features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures direct experience assessing systems for security issues through threat modeling, review, validation, or attacker-minded analysis.

levels.descriptor: No actual security assessment work is shown.
The letter signals security interest or coursework or a credential, but not real assessment practice.
The letter gives concrete evidence of threat modeling, code review, security reviews, or similar assessment work.
The letter shows repeated, structured assessment practice with attacker-minded analysis, remediation follow-through, or broad scope across systems.

features.name: Vulnerability handling automation
features.description: Captures direct ownership of tooling that classifies, routes, deduplicates, or prioritizes vulnerability reports.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling work is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in reducing security toil, but gives no direct automation example.
The letter shows direct experience building automation for vulnerability intake, triage, routing, or prioritization.
The letter details mechanics or impact such as classification, deduplication, owner mapping, or major reduction of manual queue work.

features.evidence: Python agents ... Go services constrain what they may touch
features.name: Agentic system design
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows concrete design experience with multi-step agents and explicit guardrails, which maps directly to the job's agentic tooling focus.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or agent-based system work is mentioned.
Agents are mentioned only abstractly or as a topic of interest.
The letter shows direct experience building agentic systems using agents plus backend services.
The letter explains agent architecture in detail, including autonomy boundaries, permissions, auditing, decomposition, or supervision.

features.evidence: replaced ad-hoc traversals with proper graph algorithms
features.name: Algorithmic engineering evidence
features.description: Captures how convincingly the letter demonstrates using data structures and algorithms to materially improve real systems.

levels.descriptor: No data-structure or algorithmic strength is shown.
The letter claims algorithmic ability, but gives no concrete example.
The letter gives a specific example of using a data structure or algorithm to improve a real system.
The letter shows strong, recent algorithmic judgment with clear system impact, such as redesigning a hot path, matching flow, graph logic, indexing, or streaming computation.

features.evidence: make the secure path the easy path
features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant frames security work as making secure behavior easier for product engineers rather than imposing process.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not show a developer-facing security mindset.
The letter uses generic collaboration language without showing how security should fit developer workflows.
The letter explicitly wants to help engineers adopt secure practices through tooling or defaults.
The letter presents a clear low-friction philosophy, such as secure defaults, removing process overhead, or embedding security directly into normal engineering work.

features.evidence: scale scarce security judgment across an entire company
features.name: Security-at-scale insight
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the leverage of central security automation, variant analysis, and capacity multiplication in Google's environment.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows only generic interest in backend work or security.
The letter mentions scale or foundational impact, but only in broad terms.
The letter clearly connects the role to organization-wide leverage through central tooling or automation of expert workflows.
The letter offers a strategic view of multiplying scarce security judgment, variant analysis, or team capacity across a large ecosystem.

features.name: Production delivery depth
features.description: Captures the degree of real-world software product experience conveyed through years in role and number of production systems tested, maintained, or launched.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives thin or barely qualifying evidence of production software experience.
The letter shows solid early-career production experience with at least some testing, maintenance, or launch responsibility.
The letter shows multiple years of work and several production systems launched or maintained.
The letter shows extensive experience well beyond the minimums, with repeated launches and sustained ownership of production systems.

features.name: Advanced academic training
features.description: Captures how much the letter exceeds the baseline educational requirement through advanced computer science study relevant to the role.

levels.descriptor: No degree is stated or the background is below the bachelor's level.
The letter shows a bachelor's degree or equivalent only.
The letter shows a master's degree in a relevant field.
The letter shows a doctoral degree or PhD in a relevant field.

features.name: Formal security credential
features.description: Captures whether the letter offers externally validated security training or assessment beyond self-described interest.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
The letter mentions a foundational security credential, such as Security+ or similar.
The letter mentions an advanced practical security credential, such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.name: Offensive practice
features.description: Captures active adversarial practice through capture-the-flag events or similar hands-on exercises that sharpen attacker thinking.

levels.descriptor: No offensive practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional CTF participation or light adversarial practice.
The letter shows regular offensive practice used as ongoing attacker-minded training.
The letter shows unusually serious offensive practice, such as strong competitive results or near-top placements.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures external code ownership through maintaining, releasing, or contributing to open-source projects used by others.

levels.descriptor: No open-source involvement is mentioned.
The letter shows occasional upstream patches or bugfix contributions.
The letter shows regular contribution or maintenance of a modest open-source project or library.
The letter shows stewardship of an actively used project, including review, release, or community responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical stretch and seriousness of self-directed projects outside work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
The letter mentions a small utility or lightweight side project.
The letter mentions a substantial side project with meaningful product or systems design.
The letter mentions an ambitious project chosen for hard distributed-systems, fault-tolerance, or edge-case engineering challenges.

features.name: Concrete accomplishment specificity
features.description: Captures how much the letter supports claims with specific mechanisms, examples, or outcomes rather than broad self-description.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on generic claims about being skilled or motivated.
The letter includes some specifics, but they are sparse or vague about mechanism or impact.
The letter gives several concrete examples of what was built, improved, or learned.
The letter repeatedly uses crisp, specific examples that make the applicant's contributions and judgment easy to picture.

features.evidence: software that guards other software must be built to a higher standard
features.name: Motivational distinctiveness
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents a memorable, role-relevant reason for applying rather than a generic expression of interest.

levels.descriptor: The letter uses boilerplate application language that could fit almost any software role.
The letter shows some interest in the role, but in broad interchangeable terms.
The letter gives clear role-specific motivation tied to the team's mission or the applicant's past experience.
The letter gives a memorable, thoughtful motivation that feels personal and tightly matched to this specific role.

features.name: Surface correctness
features.description: Captures proofreading quality and absence of distracting spelling or typographical errors that undermine credibility.

levels.descriptor: Frequent distracting spelling or typographical errors repeatedly undercut the letter.
Several noticeable errors are present, though the letter remains readable.
The letter is mostly clean, with at most minor isolated mistakes.
The letter is polished and essentially error-free.

features.name: Narrative cohesion
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a coherent story linking background, skills, and desired role rather than reading like a checklist.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Engineering rigor orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter signals disciplined engineering habits suited for security-critical infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives little signal about quality, testing, reliability, or maintainability.
The letter gestures at seriousness or standards, but without concrete habits or practices.
The letter clearly emphasizes dependable systems, testing, maintainability, guardrails, or careful design.
The letter strongly signals security-critical rigor, with explicit habits such as typed or tested tooling, auditable boundaries, reliability-first design, or builder-quality standards.
